page: Amazon Web Services r7i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance powered by Intel Xeon 8488C processors based on the x86_64 architecture. The server delivers 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated vCPUs operating at a 3.2 GHz clock speed, backed by 105 MB of L3 cache. It is populated with 1536.0 GB of high-frequency 5 GHz DDR5 system memory, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The platform is provisioned with 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and includes zero dedicated GPUs. It features no local NVMe storage arrays, requiring persistent block storage to be provisioned over the network, and runs directly on bare metal without a hypervisor abstraction layer.

Benchmark evaluations show upper-decile multi-core execution throughput, supported by top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU metrics. The DDR5 memory bus sustains 459.34 GB/s of uncached read throughput and 189.0 GB/s of uncached write throughput. High memory speed combined with extensive thread parallelism enables Redis to reach 187.99 million SET operations per second and achieves top-tier scores in PassMark database workloads. Furthermore, the Intel Xeon processor includes AMX and AVX-512 extensions, yielding strong prompt processing and inference capabilities for small to large CPU-driven language models alongside accelerated software compilation.

The absence of local storage makes the system reliant on network-attached storage, which introduces external I/O management considerations. In terms of cost efficiency, the high concentration of 192 threads and 1.5 TB of RAM within a single non-virtualized footprint eliminates hypervisor overhead and minimizes multi-node clustering overhead for memory-bound tasks. The r7i.metal-48xl is primarily suited for large-scale in-memory key-value databases, enterprise relational database management systems, massive parallel compilation tasks, and memory-intensive analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r7i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance featuring 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs on Intel Xeon 8488C x86_64 processors clocked at 3.2 GHz. The platform is configured with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, delivering an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. The server lacks discrete GPUs and bundled local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent file systems. Across benchmark evaluations, the instance records top-tier multi-threaded processing power, uncached read bandwidth exceeding 459 GB/s, and Redis performance of 187.99 million operations per second. Hardware support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions enables effective CPU-driven matrix operations and large language model prompt evaluation. By eliminating hypervisor overhead and delivering high memory density, r7i.metal-48xl provides a consolidated platform suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, high-concurrency enterprise relational workloads, large software builds, and extensive data processing pipelines.
